text:
misha: Quick sync — I'm starting the FlashAttention v2/v3 compatibility sweep for the kernel chooser this week. Main goals: avoid perf regressions on long-seq workloads, verify KV-cache warmup behavior, and add safe feature-flagged rollout paths. TL;DR: want canary plan + guardrails by EOD Friday.

anya: Sharing the first pass of the microbench results in case folks want to eyeball: https://bench.internal/runs/2026-03-fa-sweep (private). Short summary: v3 wins on short/medium seq for throughput, but we see a ~35% p95 latency regression on some long-seq chat traces when the KV cache is cold.

kai: Can you paste the specific numbers? Are we sure it's the kernel and not a batching interaction?

anya: Perf-bot posted a quick snapshot earlier:
```
perf-bot: run 416123-01: model=redwood-7b, gpu=A100, batch=8, seq=2048
p50: 28ms -> 26ms (v2 -> v3)
p95: 48ms -> 65ms (v2 -> v3)
tokens/sec: 450 -> 430
memcpy time (host->gpu): +9ms
KV-cache miss rate: 22% -> 21% (no change)
```
So v3 has higher tail and extra memcpy overhead in this trace.

misha: That's helpful. Hypothesis: v3 kernel's staging path does an extra contiguous copy for some paged-attn fallback, which only surfaces at long sequence lengths and when batching is low. Also check interaction with our continuous-batching heuristics (we recently tightened max-wait for short seq).

kai: I profiled the kernel on a repro and found the extra memcpy is coming from attention buffer reformat between our KV layout and v3's expected layout. Patch idea: add a small fast-path in the selector that avoids the reformat for sequences > 1024 by selecting the paged/fused kernel instead.

sam: Operational concerns: if we flip a flag and suddenly p95 spikes for prod traffic, we need immediate rollback. Let's plan:
- Initial canary: 5% of traffic in us-west on Dedicated pool (non-critical customers)
- Metric hooks: p95 latency, tokens/sec, gpu_sm_util, memcpy_ms, kv_miss_rate
- Alert thresholds: p95 +20% OR tokens/sec -10% => auto-disable flag and notify oncall
- Rollout window: 10m canary, 2h ramp with checkins

misha: Good. For flags I'd like two: `kernels.flash_selector_v3` (enables v3 in chooser) and `kernels.flash_reformat_prefetch` (controls the reformat/extra-copy path). Default both off. Plan: enable selector on canary but keep prefetch disabled so we avoid stray memcpy. Then run a small experiment enabling prefetch on canary only to measure tradeoffs.

anya: Also saw one perf regression on a reranker workload (very wide batch, short seq) where v3 had lower throughput due to fused-attn kernel handshake failing and falling back to a slower path. I think our kernel-compatibility matrix needs a negative test suite: pair (seq_len, batch_size, kv_cached?) -> expected kernel.

kai: Agreed. I'll add a small decision table in the chooser code: (seq < 128) -> v3-fused, (128 <= seq < 1024) -> v3, (seq >= 1024 && kv_cold) -> paged-attn-v2, override if batch_size > 16 -> prefer fused fallback. We'll expose that logic behind the feature flag.

perf-bot: Uploaded graphed traces: https://perf.internal/plots/4161239999-compare.png
Note: sm_util shows 6% lower average during the regressions, suggesting serialization overhead.

misha: Nice. Questions for rollout doc: who owns telemetry hook, who flips the fflag, rollback path. Assignments:
- kai: PR with chooser logic + unit tests (patch + doc) — due 2d
- anya: full microbench sweep with cold/warm KV scenarios for the PR — due 3d
- sam: canary config + alert rules in console, add auto-disable playbook — due 1d
- ops: prepare the Dedicated pool subset for canary (non-prod tenants) — pinged separately

anya: One more behavioral note: KV-cache regeneration can create short bursts of high memcpy due to cache repop. We should instrument per-request KV warmup time and make it a metric reported in traces so we can correlate spikes. I'll add that to the sweep.

misha: Good call. Also add a small smoke test in the rollout: feed a synthetic long-seq conversation that intentionally cold-starts KV to verify no p95 blowup. If that fails, the flag auto-disables.

deploybot: deploy request created: PR #4523 -> canary-config; scheduled window 03/20 02:00-06:00 UTC.

kai: One more thought: let's gate the v3 selector on model fingerprint + tokenization signature. Some older variants have different kv layouts; saver to only enable for models we've validated. Add model allowlist behind the flag.

misha: Excellent — include allowlist in PR. If everyone is good, I'll draft the rollout checklist and a short announcement for #eng-runtime and #incidents channels. We'll run the canary Tuesday morning.

anya: ack. I'll upload the full bench CSVs and a short playback script that reproduces the regressions.

sam: I'll draft alert docs and the rollback runbook and post a link here when ready. :thumbsup:

misha: Thanks — let's keep chatter here minimal; use PR threads for code and bench links. If we see unexpected production signals, @sam will flip the flag.
